author: T. R. Hamilton
title: Registration deadline for Maui County Fair Parade set for Sept. 1
text:
Registration deadline for Maui County Fair Parade set for Sept. 1
The registration deadline for the Maui County Fair Parade is noon on Tuesday, Sept. 1, according to an announcement on Aug. 19. The parade will launch the 99th Maui Fair on Thursday, Oct. 1 at 4:30 p.m., with support from Maui Land & Pineapple Company Inc. and the County of Maui.
Parade applications and participant lists must be submitted by the deadline, as space is limited and participation will be determined on a first-come, first-served basis. Applications are available online at the official fair website. All accepted participants are required to attend a mandatory meeting on Tuesday, Sept. 8 from 6–7 p.m., held at Pōmaikaʻi Elementary School Cafeteria, where staging assignments, parade rules, and admission tickets will be distributed.
The parade route will begin at UH-Maui College and travel along Kaʻahumanu Avenue before proceeding to Kanaloa Avenue, following recent years’ traditions.
Mayor Richard Bissen said, “The parade brings together ʻohana, businesses, schools, organizations and community groups to celebrate the people, traditions and community spirit that make Maui special.” He continued: “It’s an opportunity for our community to come together, share in the excitement and enjoy a cherished part of the Maui County Fair.”
This year introduces new competitive elements with participating units eligible for “Best Of” awards in five categories: Walking/Marching Unit (more than 50 participants), Walking/Marching Unit (fewer than 50 participants), Mobile Unit, Walking/Mobile Unit, and Overall.
For more information about contests or exhibitions at this year’s fair or details about volunteering or sponsorships, individuals can visit the official fair website or contact organizers directly during business hours by phone or email. Mayor Bissen led efforts for the fair’s return after a six-year hiatus; earlier this year he proposed—and received approval from the Maui County Council—for a $1.5 million General Fund appropriation supporting this event.
